chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Goods were brought to my father (peace be upon him) from Egypt, so he prepared food and invited the merchants to it. They said, 'We take it from you for 'dah' and 'dowazdah' (ten and twelve).' My father asked them, 'And how much is that?' They said, 'For every ten thousand, two thousand.' My father said to them, 'I sell you this goods for twelve thousand.' So he sold it to them through bargaining.

key_terms.دَهْ دَوَازْدَهْ: Persian terms for ten and twelve, used here to indicate a price of 12,000

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling goods through bargaining (musawamah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the permissibility of *musawamah* (bargaining) in commercial transactions, highlighting Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) clarity in distinguishing between the number of items and the total price to avoid ambiguity (*gharar*). It serves as a foundational precedent in Shia jurisprudence for transparent negotiation, emphasizing that profit derived from clear mutual consent is lawful. The narrative underscores the ethical dimension of trade, where the seller ensures the buyer fully understands the value exchanged.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There came to my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> some goods from Egypt, so he<sup>asws</sup> had some food prepared and invited the merchants to it. So they said, ‘We take it from you<sup>asws</sup> with ten, twelve (in Persian)’. So my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> said to them: ‘And how much does that happen to be?’ They said, ‘Regarding every ten thousand, two thousand’. So my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> said to them: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> hereby sell these goods to you for twelve thousand’. So he<sup>asws</sup> sold it to them, (with) a compromise’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once goods for my father came from Egypt. He (the Imam) prepared food and invited the merchants. They said, ‘We buy from you Be dah dawazdah. He (the Imam) asked, ‘How much is that?’ They replied, ‘It is two thousand on every ten thousand.’ My father said to them, ‘I sell this to you for twelve thousand.’ He (the Imam) sold it to them in the form of Musawamah (fixed price regardless of the capital).”
